en.description: A compact houseplant with broad, glossy, elliptical leaves splashed silver-green over a dark green margin, rising on short stems from a central crown. Native to the rainforest floor of the Philippines and Sulawesi.
en.reasoning: Broad elliptical leaves with a silver central splash and dark margins match Aglaonema 'Silver Bay' closely.

uses.edible: Not edible. Every part contains calcium oxalate crystals that burn the mouth and throat. Keep it away from children, cats, and dogs.
uses.medicinal: No safe traditional use. The sap irritates skin and eyes, so wash your hands after repotting.
uses.ecologicalRole: A shade-loving understory plant of Southeast Asian rainforests. Indoors it tolerates low light and is a common first houseplant.
uses.pollinatorValue: Low. It rarely flowers indoors, and its small white spathes attract few insects.
uses.waterNeeds: Moderate. Let the top of the soil dry between waterings and keep it above 15 °C.
uses.culturalUses: Prized in Chinese and Southeast Asian homes as a bringer of good fortune. 'Silver Bay' is a modern cultivar bred for its wide silver leaves.

alternatives.reasoning: Similar variegation, but dumb cane leaves are larger and more oblong on a thick cane-like stem.
